title: God's BBQ Rules: How to Make a Proper Offering
paragraphs: So, God hit up Moses from the main tent, the Tent of Meeting, and was like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites the deal. When someone wants to bring an offering to God, it's gotta be an animal from your herd or flock.'

'If you're doing a Whole-Burnt-Offering with a bull, you gotta bring a perfect one, no flaws, right to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting so God will be cool with it. You put your hand on its head, and that basically makes it your stand-in to get you right with God. Then, you take care of the bull right there in front of God. Aaron's sons, the priests, will take the blood and splash it on all sides of the Altar at the entrance. After that, you skin the offering and cut it into pieces. The priests will get a fire going on the Altar, lay out the wood, and then arrange all the parts, even the head and the fat, on the fire. Make sure to wash the insides and legs super clean. The priest will then burn the whole thing on the Altar. It's a Whole-Burnt-Offering, a gift made with fire, and it smells amazing to God.'

'Now, if your Whole-Burnt-Offering is from your flock, like a sheep or a goat, same deal: a perfect male. You handle it on the north side of the Altar, with God watching. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash the blood on all sides of the Altar. Then you cut it up, and the priest puts all the pieces, head and fat included, on the wood that's ready for the fire on the Altar. Don't forget to scrub the insides and legs. The priest offers it all up, burning it on the Altar. It's a Whole-Burnt-Offering, a gift made with fire, and it smells amazing to God.'

'And if you're bringing a bird for the Whole-Burnt-Offering, it can be a dove or a pigeon. The priest takes it to the Altar, wrings its head off, and burns it on the Altar. But first, he's gotta drain the blood on the side of the Altar, take out the gizzard and whatever's in it, and toss them on the east side of the Altar where they keep the ashes. Then, you rip it open by the wings—but don't tear it completely apart—and the priest burns it on the Altar on the wood. That's a Whole-Burnt-Offering, a gift made with fire, and it smells amazing to God.'

title: God's Favorite Snacks: The Grain Offering Guide
paragraphs: When you present a Grain-Offering to God, use the good stuff: fine flour. Pour some oil on it, add some incense, and bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. One of them will take a handful of the flour and oil, with all the incense, and burn it on the Altar as a memorial. It's a Fire-Gift, a scent that God really likes. The rest of the Grain-Offering is for Aaron and his sons—it's the most holy part of the Fire-Gifts to God.
If you're bringing a Grain-Offering of oven-baked loaves, use fine flour mixed with oil, but no yeast. Or you can offer wafers made without yeast and spread with oil.
If your Grain-Offering is cooked on a griddle, use fine flour mixed with oil but no yeast. Crumble it up and pour oil on it—that's a Grain-Offering.
If you're bringing a Grain-Offering that's deep-fried, make it with fine flour and oil.

Bring the Grain-Offering you've made from these ingredients and give it to the priest. He'll take it to the Altar, break off a memorial piece, and burn it on the Altar. It's a Fire-Gift, a fragrance that pleases God. The rest of the Grain-Offering goes to Aaron and his sons—it's a super holy part of the gifts to God.

Here's a major rule: All the Grain-Offerings you give to God must be made without yeast. You must never burn any yeast or honey as a Fire-Gift to God. You can offer them to God as a firstfruits offering, but they don't go on the Altar as a pleasing fragrance. And make sure you season every single Grain-Offering with salt. Don't forget the salt of the covenant with your God in your offerings. Present all your offerings with salt.

If you bring a Grain-Offering of firstfruits to God, bring crushed heads of new grain that have been roasted. Put oil and incense on it—it's a Grain-Offering. The priest will burn some of the mixed grain and oil with all the incense as a memorial—a Fire-Gift to God.

title: God's Guide to Peace Offerings (ft. BBQ)
paragraphs: Alright, so if you're bringing a Peace-Offering and it's from your herd, whether it's a male or female, it's gotta be perfect—no defects. You put your hand on its head, then you sacrifice it right at the entrance of the main tent. The priests, Aaron's sons, will then splash its blood on all sides of the altar. For the fire-gift part for God, you offer up all the fat that covers the guts, the two kidneys with the fat around them, and the best part of the liver. Aaron and his sons will burn all that on the altar on top of the other burnt offering that's already on the fire. It's a special gift, and God loves the smell.

If your Peace-Offering is from your flock, like a sheep, it also has to be perfect, male or female. If it's a lamb, you bring it to God, put your hand on its head, and sacrifice it in front of the main tent. Aaron's sons will splash the blood around the altar. The fire-gift for God from this offering is all its fat—the whole tail cut close to the spine, all the fat around the guts, the two kidneys with their fat, and the best part of the liver. The priest burns this on the altar. It's like a meal, a fire-gift for God.

If you're offering a goat, you bring it to God, lay your hand on its head, and sacrifice it in front of the main tent. Aaron's sons will splash the blood on the altar. The fire-gift for God is the fat covering the guts, the two kidneys with their fat, and the best part of the liver. The priest will burn all of it on the altar. It's a meal, a fire-gift that smells amazing to God.
Here's the deal: all the fat belongs to God. This is a forever rule for all your generations, no matter where you live. So, no eating the fat, and no eating the blood. Seriously, none of it.

title: Whoops! How to Apologize to God
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Yo, tell the Israelites the deal. If someone messes up without meaning to and breaks one of God's rules—you know, the stuff you're absolutely not supposed to do—here's the plan.

If it's the head priest who slips up and makes everyone else look guilty by association, he's gotta bring a perfect bull to God as an Absolution-Offering for the sin. He'll bring the bull to the entrance of the main tent in God's presence, lay his hand on the bull's head, and then slaughter it right there before God. Then he's gotta take some of the bull's blood, bring it into the Tent of Meeting, dip his finger in it, and sprinkle some of it seven times before God, right in front of the curtain of the Sanctuary. He needs to smear some of the blood on the horns of the Altar of Fragrant Incense that's in the Tent of Meeting. The rest of the bull's blood? He just pours it out at the base of the big outdoor Altar of Whole-Burnt-Offering. He has to remove all the fat from the bull—the fat that covers the organs, the two kidneys and the fat around them, and the lobe of the liver. It's the same procedure as when they take the fat from the bull for a Peace-Offering. Finally, he burns all this on the Altar of Burnt Offering. Everything else—the bull's hide, all the meat, its head, legs, organs, and guts—he has to take it all outside the camp to a clean spot where they dump the ashes and burn it all on a wood fire.

If the whole community messes up by accident, straying from one of God's rules that you're not supposed to break, they're technically guilty even if nobody realizes it at first. When they do figure out the sin they committed, the whole crew has to bring a bull as an Absolution-Offering and present it at the Tent of Meeting. The elders of the community will lay their hands on the bull's head in God's presence, and one of them will slaughter it before God. The head priest will then bring some of the blood into the Tent of Meeting, dip his finger in it, and sprinkle it seven times before God, right in front of the curtain. He'll smear some of the blood on the horns of the Altar inside the Tent of Meeting and pour the rest of it at the base of the outdoor Altar of Whole-Burnt-Offering. He'll remove all the fat and burn it on the Altar. He'll follow the exact same steps with this bull as he did with the bull for his own offering. The priest makes things right for them, and they are forgiven. Then they'll take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just like they burned the first one. It's the Absolution-Offering for the whole community.

When a leader sins without meaning to, breaking one of the commands of his God that shouldn't be broken, he's guilty. When he realizes the sin he's committed, he has to bring a male goat with no defects as his offering, lay his hand on the goat's head, and slaughter it in the same place they slaughter the Whole-Burnt-Offering in God's presence—it's an Absolution-Offering. The priest will then take some of the blood from the offering with his finger, smear it on the horns of the Altar of Whole-Burnt-Offering, and pour the rest at the base of the Altar. He'll burn all its fat on the Altar, just like with the fat of the Peace-Offering.
The priest makes things right for him because of his sin, and he's forgiven.

When a regular person from the community sins by accident, straying from one of God's commands that shouldn't be broken, they're guilty. When they're made aware of their sin, they have to bring a female goat with no defects and offer it for their sin, lay their hand on the head of the Absolution-Offering, and slaughter it at the place of the Whole-Burnt-Offering. The priest will take some of its blood with his finger, smear it on the horns of the Altar of Whole-Burnt-Offering, and pour the rest at the base of the Altar. Finally, he'll take out all the fat, just like with the Peace-Offerings, and burn it on the Altar for a smell that pleases God.
This way, the priest makes things right for them, and they're forgiven.

If someone brings a lamb for an Absolution-Offering, they have to present a female without any defects, lay their hand on the head of the offering, and slaughter it at the same place they slaughter the Whole-Burnt-Offering. The priest will take some of the blood from the offering with his finger, smear it on the horns of the Altar of Burnt-Offering, and pour the rest at the base of the Altar. He has to remove all the fat, the same way they do for the lamb of the Peace-Offering. Finally, the priest will burn it on the Altar on top of the other gifts to God.
This way, the priest makes things right for them on account of their sin, and they're forgiven."

title: Whoops, I Sinned... Now What? 😬
paragraphs: Alright, so check it. If you see something messed up happen and you know about it, but you don't step up to be a witness, you're gonna be held responsible. That's on you.

Or, like, if you accidentally touch something gross and unclean, like a dead animal or whatever, and you don't even realize it at first... well, you're still technically contaminated and guilty. Intense, right?
Same deal if you touch some kind of human uncleanness without knowing. The moment you realize it, boom, you're guilty.
And if you make some impulsive promise, like just blurting out an oath to do something, good or bad, without really thinking? If you realize it later, yep, you're guilty for that too.
So when you figure out you're guilty, you gotta confess the sin right away. Then, you bring a female lamb or a goat as a penalty to God. It's called an Absolution-Offering.
This is how the priest will make things right for your sin.

But what if you're broke and can't afford a lamb? No worries. You can bring two doves or two pigeons to God instead. One is for the Absolution-Offering, and the other is for a Whole-Burnt-Offering. You give them to the priest, and he'll offer the first one for your sin, wringing its neck but not cutting it all the way off. He'll splash some of its blood on the altar and drain the rest at the bottom. That's the Absolution-Offering. Then he'll offer the second bird as a Whole-Burnt-Offering, following all the steps.
And just like that, the priest makes things right for your sin, and you're forgiven. Honestly, that's a pretty good deal.

Okay, but what if you can't even afford two birds? Then you bring two quarts of fine flour for your Absolution-Offering. But don't add any oil or incense to it, 'cause this is serious business. You bring it to the priest, he takes a handful as a memorial, and burns it on the altar with the other gifts for God. It's an Absolution-Offering.
That's how the priest will make atonement for any of these sins you've committed, and you're forgiven. The rest of the offering goes to the priest, just like with the Grain-Offering.

Then God told Moses, "If someone messes up and unknowingly sins against any of God's holy things, they have to bring a perfect ram from their flock as a penalty. The ram's value is set in shekels, and it's for a Compensation-Offering. They also have to add an extra twenty percent to make up for the holy thing they messed up and give it all to the priest.
This way, the priest will make things right for them with the ram, and they're forgiven.

And if anyone sins by breaking one of God's commandments without realizing it, the second they do realize it, they're responsible. They have to bring a perfect ram to the priest, valued for a Compensation-Offering.
And the priest will make atonement for the mistake they made without knowing, and they'll be forgiven. It's a Compensation-Offering, 'cause they were definitely guilty before God. Seriously.

title: Spiritual Hacks: The Right Way to Say Sorry to God
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, "Yo, if someone messes up and breaks my trust by scamming their neighbor—like if they were supposed to be watching something for a friend and they lie about it, or they straight up rob or cheat someone, or they find something someone lost and then lie and swear they didn't... basically any of the usual ways people sin... if they do that and get caught, they have to give back whatever they stole or scammed. Plus, they gotta add an extra 20% on top and give it all back to the person they wronged. And on that same day, they have to bring a special offering to me, a perfect ram, to show they're sorry.
Then the priest will make things right for them with me, and they'll be forgiven for whatever they did that made them guilty.

God also told Moses, "Give Aaron and his sons the rundown on the burnt offering. It has to stay on the altar all night until the morning, with the fire going the whole time. In the morning, the priest needs to put on his special linen clothes, right down to his underwear, and clean up the ashes from the offering. He puts the ashes next to the altar, then changes his clothes and takes the ashes to a clean spot outside the camp. The fire on the altar has to keep burning, no excuses. Every morning, they need to add more wood, put the offering on it, and burn the fat from the peace offering on top. Seriously, that fire can never go out.

And here's the scoop on the grain offering. Aaron's sons have to present it to me right in front of the altar. The priest scoops up a handful of the flour, oil, and incense, and burns it on the altar. It's like a little reminder that smells awesome to me. Aaron and his sons get to eat the rest, but it has to be bread made without yeast, and they have to eat it in a holy place, the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. No baking it with yeast, that's a hard rule. I've set it aside as their cut of the gifts. It's super holy, just like the offerings for forgiveness. Any guy in Aaron's family line can eat it. This is a forever rule about my gifts. Anyone who touches these offerings has to be holy, for real.

God also told Moses, "When Aaron and his sons get anointed, they have to bring me an offering: two quarts of fine flour, half in the morning, half in the evening. Cook it on a griddle with oil, mix it up good, and then offer it up in crumbles. It smells great to me. The son of Aaron who takes over for him has to offer it too—that's a fixed rule. The whole thing gets burned. Every grain offering from a priest has to be completely burned; they can't eat any of it.

Then God said to Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons the rules for the forgiveness offering. They have to slaughter it in the same place they do the big burnt offering. It's super holy. The priest in charge gets to eat it in a holy place, the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. Anyone who touches any of the meat has to be holy. If blood splatters on a piece of clothing, it has to be washed in a holy place. If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, you have to smash the pot. If it was a bronze pot, you have to scrub it clean and rinse it with water. Any guy from the priest families can eat it; it's that holy. But if the blood from a forgiveness offering is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make things right in the Sanctuary, no one can eat it. It has to be burned."

title: God's BBQ Rules: The Lowdown on Offerings
paragraphs: “Alright, here are the deets for the Make-It-Right Offering. This one is next-level holy. You gotta sacrifice the Make-It-Right Offering in the same spot as the big Whole-Burnt-Offering. Splash its blood on all sides of the altar. Then, offer up all the fat parts: the fat tail, the fat covering the guts, the two kidneys and the fat around them, plus the lobe of the liver. The priest will burn all that on the altar as a special gift to God. That's a Make-It-Right Offering. Any guy from the priest's family can eat the meat, but it has to be eaten in a holy place because, again, it's super sacred.

“Basically, the Make-It-Right Offering and the Forgiveness Offering have the same rules. The offering belongs to the priest who handles the ceremony. Also, the priest who presents a Whole-Burnt-Offering for someone gets to keep the animal hide. And any Grain-Offering—whether it's baked, cooked in a pan, or on a griddle—belongs to the priest who offers it. It's his. Every Grain-Offering, dry or mixed with oil, is shared equally among all of Aaron's sons.

“Now, for the Peace-Offering you bring to God. If you're bringing it to say thanks, you need to include some unraised bread mixed with oil, some unraised wafers with oil spread on them, and some well-kneaded cakes of fine flour mixed with oil. Along with your Thank-You Peace-Offering, you also have to bring some loaves of bread made with yeast. Bring one of each kind as a special contribution to God; that part goes to the priest who splashes the blood of the Peace-Offering. You have to eat the meat from your Thank-You Peace-Offering on the same day it's offered. Don't leave any leftovers for the morning.

“If your offering is a Promise-Offering or a Just-Because-You-Want-To Offering, you can eat the meat on the day it's sacrificed, and if there are leftovers, you can eat them the next day. But any meat that's still around on the third day has to be burned. If you eat any meat from the Peace-Offering on the third day, it doesn't count. It won't do you any good—it's considered nasty. And whoever eats it will have to face the consequences. Also, don't eat any meat that's touched something spiritually unclean; burn it. Any other meat can be eaten by people who are spiritually clean. But if you're not clean and you eat meat from a Peace-Offering to God, you're cut off from the community. And if you touch anything unclean—whether it's from a person, an animal, or some gross object—and then go and eat from a Peace-Offering, you're totally cut off from the community.”

God told Moses, “Tell the Israelites: Don't eat the fat from cattle, sheep, or goats. The fat from an animal that died on its own or was killed by wild animals can be used for other stuff, but you absolutely cannot eat it. If you eat fat from an animal that could have been a gift to God, you'll be cut off from the community. And no matter where you live, don't eat blood, whether it's from a bird or an animal. If you eat any blood, you're cut off from the community.”

God then said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites this: When you bring a Peace-Offering to God, you have to bring a part of it as a special gift to God, with your own hands. Bring the fat with the breast, and wave the breast before God as a Wave-Offering. The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but Aaron and his sons get to keep the breast. You also give the right thigh from your Peace-Offerings to the priest as a contribution. The son of Aaron who offers the blood and fat of the Peace-Offering gets the right thigh as his share. From the Peace-Offerings of Israel, I'm giving the breast from the Wave-Offering and the thigh from the Contribution-Offering to Aaron the priest and his sons. This is their permanent share from the people of Israel.”

From the day they were appointed to serve as God's priests, Aaron and his sons were set to receive these portions from the gifts given to God. This is what God commanded the Israelites to give the priests from the day they were anointed. It's a fixed rule for all time.

So, those are the instructions for the Whole-Burnt-Offering, the Grain-Offering, the Forgiveness-Offering, the Make-It-Right Offering, the Ordination-Offering, and the Peace-Offering, which God gave to Moses on Mount Sinai on the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to God in the Sinai wilderness.

title: Priest Initiation Ceremony GOES WILD
paragraphs: Alright, so God hits up Moses and is like, 'Yo, grab your brother Aaron and his sons. Also, get all the special priest outfits, the anointing oil, the bull for the big apology offering, those two rams, and the basket of flatbread. Then, get everyone in the community to pull up to the entrance of the main tent.' So Moses, being the good dude he is, does exactly what God says, and everyone gathers around.
Moses gets everyone's attention and says, 'Aight people, listen up! We're about to do what God told us to do.'

Then Moses brings Aaron and his sons out and gives them a good wash. He gets Aaron dressed in this long shirt thingy, ties a sash around it, and then puts a robe over that. Next up is the Ephod, which is like a special vest, and he tightens it with a cool woven belt so it fits just right. He puts the Breastpiece on him, and inside it, he slides in the Urim and Thummim – these two mysterious objects. To top it all off, he puts a turban on Aaron's head with a gold plate on the front, the holy crown. All of this was exactly what God told Moses to do.

Moses then takes the anointing oil and basically makes the whole tent and everything inside it holy. He sprinkles the oil on the altar seven times, anointing the altar and all its tools, the washbasin, and its stand, making them all sacred. Then, he pours some of the oil on Aaron's head, officially setting him apart for his new role as head priest.
Next, Moses gets Aaron's sons all dressed up. He puts tunics on them, belts them up, and gives them some cool caps to wear, just like God said.

Moses then brings out the bull for the 'my bad' offering. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head, and then Moses slaughters it. He takes some of the blood and smears it on the horns of the altar to make it pure. The rest of the blood he pours out at the bottom of the altar. This whole process makes the altar holy so that people can be forgiven for their sins there. Moses takes all the fat from the bull's insides, the liver, and the two kidneys and burns it all on the altar. But the rest of the bull—the hide, the meat, and the guts—he burns outside the camp, just like God told him to.

Then, Moses brings up the first ram for the burnt offering. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head, and Moses slaughters it, splashing the blood on all sides of the altar. He cuts the ram into pieces and burns the head, the pieces, and the fat. After washing the insides and the legs, he burns the whole ram on the altar. This was a burnt offering, and it smelled amazing—a gift to God, just as he was told.

Next up is the second ram, the one for the ordination ceremony. Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head, and Moses slaughters it. He takes some of its blood and puts it on Aaron's right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe. He does the same thing for Aaron's sons. The rest of the blood he throws against the sides of the altar. He takes all the fatty parts, the liver, the kidneys, and the right thigh. From the basket of flatbread, he takes one loaf made with oil and one wafer, and puts them on top of the fat and the thigh. He puts all of this in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and they wave it before God as a special offering. Then Moses takes it all back and burns it on the altar. This was the ordination offering, and it was a gift that smelled great to God. Moses also takes the breast of the ram and waves it before God; that part was his share, just as God had commanded.

Moses then takes some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkles it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. This made them and their priestly garments officially holy.

Finally, Moses tells Aaron and his sons, 'Boil the meat at the entrance of the main tent and eat it there with the bread from the ordination basket, just like I told you. Burn any leftovers. And listen, you can't leave the entrance of the tent for seven days. That's how long your ordination takes. What we did today was God's command to make things right for you. So, you gotta stay at the entrance of the tent, day and night, for seven days straight. Make sure you do everything God requires, or you'll die. For real, this is what I was commanded.'
And so, Aaron and his sons did everything that God had commanded through Moses.

title: God's Glory Unleashed! Fire from Heaven!
paragraphs: Alright, so on day eight, Moses gets Aaron, his sons, and all the top leaders of Israel together. He tells Aaron, "Yo, grab a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Make sure they're perfect, no flaws, and offer them up to God."

"Then, tell everyone else in Israel to get a male goat for their sin offering, a calf and a lamb (both a year old and perfect) for a burnt offering, and a bull and a ram for a peace offering. They need to sacrifice these to God with a grain offering mixed with oil. Why? Because God's gonna show up for you all today. It's gonna be epic."

So, they brought everything Moses ordered to the main tent. The whole crew gathered around and stood there before God. Moses was like, "This is what God told you to do, so you can see His awesome glory appear right before your eyes."

Moses then tells Aaron, "Step up to the altar. Do your sin offering and your burnt offering. This is to make things right for you and for everyone else. Then, do the offering for the people to make things right for them, exactly like God said."

Aaron walked up to the altar and sacrificed the calf for his own sin offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he dipped his finger in it and put some on the corners of the altar. He poured the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar. Then he burned the fat, the kidneys, and part of the liver on the altar, just like God told Moses. The meat and the skin? He burned those outside the camp.

Next up, he sacrificed the burnt offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it on all sides of the altar. They gave him the pieces and the head, and he burned them on the altar too. He washed the guts and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering.

Then it was time for the people's offerings. Aaron took the goat for the people's sin offering, sacrificed it, and offered it up just like he did the first one. He did the burnt offering the same way as before. He presented the grain offering by taking a handful and burning it on the altar with the morning's burnt offering. He also sacrificed the bull and the ram, which were the peace offerings for the people. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it on all sides of the altar. The fatty parts from the bull and the ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver—they put on the breasts, and Aaron burned all of it on the altar. Aaron then waved the breasts and the right thigh before God as a special offering, just like God commanded.

Finally, Aaron lifted his hands over the people and blessed them. After finishing all the offerings—the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering—he came down from the altar. Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and then BAM! The glory of God appeared to everyone. Fire shot out from God and completely burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When everyone saw it, they went wild, cheering and then falling to the ground in awe.

title: Playing With Fire Before God Goes Wrong
paragraphs: So on the same day, Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu, grabbed their censers, threw in some hot coals and incense, and offered some 'strange' fire to God—something God totally didn't ask for. Then, whoosh, fire blazed out from God and completely torched them. They died right there in God's presence.
Moses told Aaron, "This is what God meant when he said,
'To the one who comes near me, I will show myself holy; Before all the people, I will show my glory.'
Aaron was just silent.

Moses then called for Mishael and Elzaphan, who were the sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. He told them, "Come on, you need to carry your dead cousins outside the camp, away from the Sanctuary." So they came and carried them out of the camp, just like Moses said.

Then Moses laid down the law for Aaron and his other sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: "Don't you dare show any signs of mourning—no messy hair, no torn clothes. If you do, you'll die too, and God will be angry with everyone. Your relatives, basically all the people of Israel, will do the mourning for the ones God just destroyed by fire. And don't even think about leaving the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, or you'll die, because you've got God's special anointing oil on you."
And they did exactly what Moses told them.

God then gave Aaron these instructions: "When you go into the Tent of Meeting, you and your sons are not to drink any wine or strong drink. If you do, you'll die. This is a permanent rule for all generations to come. You have to know the difference between what's holy and what's common, what's clean and what's unclean. You need to teach the people of Israel all the rules that God has given them through Moses."

Moses then spoke to Aaron and his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the leftover grain offering from the fire-gifts for God, make it without yeast, and eat it next to the altar, because it's super holy. Eat it in the Holy Place, because it's your share and your sons' share from the fire-gifts for God. That's what God commanded me. Also, you, your sons, and your daughters get to eat the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution offering in a clean place. These are your share from the peace offerings of the Israelites. Bring the thigh and the breast with the fat pieces of the fire-gifts and lift them up as a wave offering. This will be the regular share for you and your kids, just as God ordered."

But when Moses checked on the goat for the sin offering, he found out it had been burned up. He got pretty mad at Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and was like, "Why didn't you eat the sin offering in the Holy Place? It's most holy! It was given to you to take away the community's guilt by making things right for them before God. Since its blood wasn't brought into the Holy Place, you were supposed to eat the goat in the Sanctuary, just like I commanded."

Aaron replied to Moses, "Look. They just sacrificed their sin offering and burnt offering before God today, and you see what happened to me—I lost two sons. Do you really think God would have been happy if I had eaten the sin offering today?"
When Moses heard that, he was like, "Fair enough," and accepted it.

title: God's Official Food Guide: What's In and What's Out
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and Aaron and was like, "Alright, listen up. Tell the Israelites the deal with animals. Here’s what you can and can’t eat.

So, any animal with a split hoof that also chews its cud is fair game. But, and this is a big but, if it only does one of those things, it's a no-go. Like, camels chew their cud, but their hooves aren't split, so they're out. Rock badgers? Same deal, cud-chewers, no split hooves—unclean. Rabbits too, they chew cud but don't have the right feet, so they're off the menu. And pigs? They've got the split hooves, but they don't chew cud, so they're unclean. Don't even think about eating their meat, and don't even touch their dead bodies. They're just not for you.

Now for all the stuff living in the water. If it has fins and scales, you're good to go. But if it's missing either fins or scales, whether it's a tiny creature in a stream or some huge monster in the ocean, you gotta steer clear. Seriously, find them disgusting. Don't eat them, and don't even mess with their dead bodies. Anything in the water without fins and scales is detestable to you.

And here's the list of birds you need to avoid. Don't eat them, they're detestable: eagles, vultures, ospreys, kites, all types of falcons, all ravens, ostriches, nighthawks, sea gulls, all hawks, owls, cormorants, ibises, water hens, pelicans, Egyptian vultures, storks, all herons, hoopoes, and bats.

Flying insects that walk on all fours? Super gross, avoid them. But there's an exception. You can eat the ones with jointed legs for hopping, like locusts, katydids, crickets, and grasshoppers. All other four-legged flying insects are off-limits.

If you touch the dead body of any of these unclean animals, you're considered spiritually unclean until evening. And if you have to carry one of their carcasses, you have to wash your clothes and you're still unclean until evening.
Any animal with a hoof that isn't completely split, or that doesn't chew cud, is unclean for you. If you touch its dead body, you become unclean.

Any four-footed animal that walks on its paws is unclean. If you touch its dead body, you're unclean until evening. If you have to carry its carcass, you have to wash your clothes and you're still unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.

As for the little critters that crawl on the ground, these are the ones you need to avoid: weasels, rats, all types of lizards, geckos, monitor lizards, wall lizards, skinks, and chameleons. These crawling things are unclean. If you touch one of them after it's dead, you're spiritually unclean until evening. If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing becomes unclean, no matter what it is—wood, cloth, leather, whatever. You have to put it in water, and it stays unclean until evening, then it's clean again. If a dead critter falls into a clay pot, everything in that pot is now unclean, and you have to smash the pot. Any food that could have been eaten becomes unclean if water from that pot touches it, and any drink in that pot is also unclean. Anything a carcass falls on becomes unclean. An oven or a pot has to be broken. They're unclean and you have to treat them that way. But a spring or a cistern where you collect water stays clean. Still, if you touch one of the carcasses in it, you become unclean. If a carcass falls on seeds you were going to plant, the seeds are still clean. But if the seeds were wet and a carcass falls on them, then they're unclean.

If one of the animals you're allowed to eat dies on its own, anyone who touches the body is unclean until evening. If you eat any of its meat, you have to wash your clothes and you're unclean until evening. If you carry its body, you have to wash your clothes and you're unclean until evening.

Crawling things are disgusting, so don't eat them. Seriously, don't eat anything that crawls on the ground, whether it's on its belly, on all fours, or has a ton of feet. They're just nasty. Don't make yourselves unclean or defiled by them, because I am your God.
I need you to be holy because I am holy. Don't make yourselves unclean with any of these crawling creatures. I'm the God who brought you out of Egypt. Be holy, because I am holy.

So there you have it. These are the rules for animals, birds, fish, and all the crawling things. You have to know the difference between what's clean and what's unclean, between the animals you can eat and the ones you can't.

title: The Post-Baby Glow Up
paragraphs: So God hit up Moses and was like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites the deal. When a woman has a baby boy, she's considered 'unclean' for seven days, kinda like when she's on her period. Then, on day eight, the baby boy gets circumcised. After that, the mom has to chill at home for 33 more days to get purified from all the bleeding. She can't touch any holy stuff or go to the main holy place until she's all good. And if she has a baby girl, she's 'unclean' for fourteen days, just like her period. Then she has to stay home for another 66 days to get purified.'

'Okay, so when her purification time is up, whether she had a boy or a girl, she's gotta bring a one-year-old lamb for a big offering and a pigeon or dove for a 'my bad' offering to the priest at the entrance of the main tent. The priest will offer it to God to make things right for her. Then, boom, she's officially clean from all the baby-related bleeding.'
'So yeah, that's the rundown for any woman who has a baby, boy or girl.'

'But what if she's broke and can't afford a whole lamb? No worries. She can bring two doves or two pigeons instead. One is for the big offering, and the other is for the 'my bad' offering. The priest will make things right for her, and she'll be all clean.'

title: That's a Nasty Rash! Skin Problems 101
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and Aaron and said, “Alright, listen up. If someone gets a weird swelling, blister, or a shiny spot on their skin that looks like it could be a serious infection, you gotta bring them to Aaron the priest or one of his sons.

The priest will check out the sore. If the hair in the sore has turned white and it looks like it's deeper than just the skin, that’s a serious, contagious skin disease. After the priest checks it, he’s gotta declare that person ‘unclean.’

But if the shiny spot is white but just on the surface, and the hair hasn't turned white, the priest will put the person in quarantine for a week. On day seven, the priest checks again. If he thinks the sore is the same and hasn't spread, he'll keep them in quarantine for another seven days. Then, on that seventh day, he’ll check them one more time. If the sore has faded and hasn't spread, the priest will say they're 'clean'—it's just a minor rash. The person can go home, wash their clothes, and they're good to go. But, plot twist, if the rash starts spreading *after* they've been declared clean, they have to go back to the priest. He'll check it again, and if it has spread, he'll have to say they're 'unclean' because it's a serious, contagious infection.

Whenever someone has a gnarly, infectious skin thing, you have to bring them to the priest. The priest will check them out. If there's a white swelling, the hair is turning white, and there's an open sore in the middle of it, it's a chronic skin disease. The priest will just straight up declare them 'unclean.' No need for quarantine this time because it's already obvious. But if the disease breaks out and covers their whole body, from head to toe, the priest will do a full check. If the disease covers the entire body, he'll actually declare the person 'clean.' Since it's all turned white, they're clean. But if there are open, oozy sores, they're unclean. The priest will see the open sores and declare them unclean. Those open sores are the proof of a serious skin disease. However, if the open sores dry up and turn white, the person has to go back to the priest. He'll re-examine them, and if the sores have turned white, the priest will pronounce them 'clean.' They're clean.

If someone has a boil that heals, but then a white swelling or a reddish-white shiny spot shows up where the boil was, they have to go show the priest. He'll check it out. If it looks like it's gone deep into the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest will declare them 'unclean.' It's a serious skin disease that broke out from the boil. But if the check-up shows no white hair, it's only skin-deep, and it has faded, the priest will quarantine them for seven days. If it spreads during that week, the priest will diagnose them as 'unclean.' It's infectious. But if the shiny spot stays the same and doesn't spread, it's just a scar from the boil. The priest will say they're 'clean.'

If someone gets a burn and the raw part turns into a reddish-white or white shiny spot, the priest has to check it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and it looks deeper than the skin, a serious skin disease has popped up in the burn area. The priest will declare them 'unclean'; it's a serious, contagious skin disease. But if the examination shows no white hair and it doesn't look too deep but has faded, the priest will quarantine them for seven days. On the seventh day, he'll check again. If it has spread by then, the priest will diagnose them as 'unclean'; it's a serious, contagious skin disease. If the shiny spot has stayed the same, hasn't spread, but has faded, it's just swelling from the burn. The priest will declare them 'clean'; it's just a burn scar.

If a man or woman gets a sore on their head or chin, the priest will check it out. If it looks like it's under the skin and the hair in it is thin and yellow, he'll pronounce them 'unclean.' It's an itchy, infectious skin disease. But if he checks the itch and finds it's only skin-deep with no black hair in it, he'll quarantine them for seven days. On the seventh day, he'll re-examine the sore. If the itch hasn't spread, there's no yellow hair, and it looks like it's just on the surface, the person has to shave, but not the itchy spot. The priest will send them back to quarantine for another week. If the itch still hasn't spread and seems only skin-deep, the priest will declare them 'clean.' They can go home, wash their clothes, and they're good. But if the itch spreads *after* being declared clean, the priest has to check it again. If it has spread, he doesn't even need to look for yellow hair; they're 'unclean.' But if he sees the itch is unchanged and black hair is growing back, the itch is healed. The person is clean, and the priest will say so.
When a man or woman gets shiny or white shiny spots on their skin, the priest is to check it out. If the spots are a dull white, it's just a rash. The person is clean.

When a man starts losing his hair and goes bald, he's clean. If he loses hair from his forehead, he's just bald, and he's clean. But if he gets a reddish-white sore on his scalp or forehead, it means a serious skin disease is breaking out. The priest has to examine it. If the swollen sore is reddish-white and looks like a serious skin disease, then he has one and is 'unclean.' The priest has to declare him unclean because of the sore on his head.

Anyone with a serious skin disease has to wear torn clothes, let their hair be a mess, cover their mouth, and yell, 'Unclean! Unclean!' As long as they have the sores, they're considered unclean. They have to live by themselves, outside the main camp.

Now for clothes. If clothing—wool or linen, woven or knitted, or even leather—gets a patch of serious fungus, and the spot is greenish or rusty, that's a bad sign. Show it to the priest. The priest will check the spot and then lock the item away for seven days. On the seventh day, he'll check it again. If the spot has spread, it's a persistent fungus, and the item is 'unclean.' He has to burn it. Because the fungus is persistent and contaminating, it has to be burned. But if the priest checks and the spot hasn't spread, he'll tell the owner to wash the item, and he'll lock it away for another seven days. He'll check it again after it's been washed. If the spot looks the same, even if it hasn't spread, it's still 'unclean.' Burn it, doesn't matter if the fungus is on the front or the back. If, when the priest checks, the spot has faded after washing, he is to tear that piece out of the garment. But if it shows up again, it's a fresh outbreak—throw whatever has the spot on it into the fire. If the garment is washed and the spot is gone, wash it a second time, and then it's 'clean.'
So yeah, those are the rules for dealing with fungus spots on clothes or leather, for deciding if they're 'clean' or 'unclean.'

title: God's Ultimate Guide to Getting Clean
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, “Alright, here’s the protocol for someone with a gnarly skin disease when it’s time for them to get clean. First, they gotta be brought to the priest. The priest will check them out outside the main camp. If the person’s actually healed up, the priest will call for two live, clean birds, some cedar wood, a scarlet string, and a hyssop branch for the cleansing ceremony. He’ll have one of the birds sacrificed over a clay pot with fresh water in it. Then, the priest will take the live bird, the cedar, the scarlet string, and the hyssop, and dip all of it in the blood of the bird that was just killed over the fresh water. He’ll sprinkle the person getting cleansed seven times and officially declare them clean. To finish, he’ll let the live bird fly off into an open field. The person who’s now clean has to wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and take a full bath. After all that, they’re officially clean. They can come back into the camp, but they have to crash outside their own tent for a week. On the seventh day, they have to shave everything again—head, beard, eyebrows, all of it. Then they wash their clothes and bathe again. Now they’re totally clean.

“The next day, day eight, he’s gotta bring two perfect male lambs and a one-year-old perfect female lamb, plus about six quarts of fine flour mixed with oil. The priest who gives the all-clear will present the person and their offerings to God at the entrance of the main tent. The priest will take one of the male lambs and the pint of oil for a Compensation-Offering and lift them up as a special wave offering to God. He’ll then sacrifice the lamb in the holy area where they do the other offerings, because this offering is super holy and belongs to the priest. The priest will then take some of the blood from that offering and dab it on the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe of the person being cleansed. After that, he’ll pour some oil into his own left palm and, with his right finger, sprinkle some of it seven times before God. The priest will then put some of that oil on the same spots—right earlobe, right thumb, right big toe—right on top of the blood from the offering. The rest of the oil goes on the person’s head to make things right for them with God.

“Finally, the priest will do the Absolution-Offering to make things right for the person getting cleansed from their impurity, then do the Whole-Burnt-Offering and the Grain-Offering on the altar. He’s made things right for him. He’s clean.

“If the person is poor and can’t afford all that, they can bring one male lamb as a Compensation-Offering to be waved to make things right, along with a couple of quarts of fine flour mixed with oil for a Grain-Offering, a pint of oil, and two doves or pigeons that they can afford—one for an Absolution-Offering and the other for a Whole-Burnt-Offering.

“On the eighth day, he brings all this to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting in front of God. The priest will take the lamb for the Compensation-Offering and a pint of oil and wave them before God as a Wave-Offering. He’ll sacrifice the lamb, take some of its blood, and put it on the person’s right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe. The priest will pour some oil into his left palm and sprinkle it seven times before God with his right finger. He’ll then put some of that oil from his palm on the same places he put the blood—the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe. The rest of the oil goes on the person’s head to make things right for them with God.

“Last up, he’ll sacrifice the doves or pigeons he could afford, one as an Absolution-Offering and the other as a Whole-Burnt-Offering with the Grain-Offering. By doing all this, the priest makes things right for the person being cleansed before God.”
These are the rules for anyone with a serious skin disease who can’t afford the standard offerings for their cleansing.

God then said to Moses and Aaron, “When you get to Canaan, the land I’m giving you, if I put a serious fungus in a house there, the owner has to go tell the priest, ‘Yo, I think I’ve got some kind of fungus in my house.’ The priest has to order everyone to clear out the house until he can come check it out, so nothing inside gets declared unclean. When the priest comes and sees the fungus on the walls, and it’s got greenish or rusty spots that look like they go deep into the wall, he’s gotta walk out and lock up the house for seven days. On the seventh day, he’ll come back for another look. If the fungus has spread, he has to order the infected stones to be ripped out and thrown in a dump outside the city. He needs to have the whole inside of the house scraped down, and all the plaster that’s removed gets tossed in the same dump. Then they have to replace the stones and replaster the whole house.

“If the fungus comes back after all that—after the stones were replaced and the house was scraped and plastered—the priest has to come check it again. If it has spread, it’s a super nasty fungus. The house is basically contaminated. It has to be torn down—all the stones, wood, and plaster get hauled to the dump outside the city. Anyone who even steps inside the house while it’s on lockdown is considered unclean until evening. Anyone who sleeps or eats in that house has to wash their clothes.

“But, if the priest comes, checks it out, and sees that the fungus hasn't spread after the replastering, he’ll declare the house clean; the fungus is gone. He’ll then purify the house by taking two birds, cedar wood, a scarlet string, and hyssop. He’ll sacrifice one bird over a clay pot with fresh water. Then he’ll take the cedar, hyssop, scarlet string, and the live bird, dip them in the blood of the dead bird and the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times. He’s cleansing the house with the bird’s blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar, the hyssop, and the scarlet string. Finally, he’ll let the live bird go free in a field outside the city. He has made things right for the house; the house is clean.

“So yeah, these are the steps for any kind of serious skin disease or itch, for mildew or fungus on clothes or in a house, and for any swelling, blister, or shiny spot, to figure out when it’s unclean and when it’s clean. These are the official rules for infectious skin diseases and fungus.”

title: God's Rules on Bodily Fluids
paragraphs: Alright, so God hit up Moses and Aaron and was like, 'Yo, tell the Israelites this: If a guy has some kind of discharge from his private parts, that stuff is considered unclean. It doesn't matter if it's a slow leak or a total blockage, he's unclean the whole time it's happening.'

Any bed he sleeps in? Unclean. Anything he sits on? Also unclean. If you touch his bed, or sit where he sat, or even touch the guy himself, you've gotta wash your clothes and take a shower. And you're considered unclean until nighttime.

If the guy with the discharge spits on a clean person, that person has to wash their clothes and shower, and they're unclean until evening. Any saddle he rides on is unclean. Whoever touches anything that was under him becomes unclean until evening. Anyone who carries something he was on has to wash their clothes and shower; they're unclean until evening. If the guy with the discharge touches someone without washing his hands first, the person he touched has to wash their clothes and shower; they're unclean until evening.
If a clay pot is touched by someone with a discharge, you have to smash it. If it's a wooden thing, just rinse it with water.

When a guy with a discharge gets better, he has to count seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and shower in running water. Then he's clean. On the eighth day, he needs to get two doves or two pigeons and go to God at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and give them to the priest. The priest then offers one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make things right for him with God because of his discharge.

If a guy has an emission of semen, he has to shower his whole body; he's unclean until evening. Any clothes or leather thing that gets semen on it has to be washed; it stays unclean until evening. When a guy and a girl sleep together and he has an emission, they both have to wash with water; they're unclean until evening.

When a woman has her period, the impurity lasts for seven days. Anyone who touches her is unclean until evening. Everything she lies or sits on during her period is unclean. Anyone who touches her bed or anything she sat on has to wash their clothes and shower; they're unclean until evening.
If a guy sleeps with her and her menstrual blood gets on him, he's unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on becomes unclean.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for a long time, but it's not her period, or if it continues after her period, she's unclean just like she is during her period. Every bed she lies on and everything she sits on during that time becomes unclean, just like during her period. Anyone who touches these things becomes unclean and has to wash their clothes and shower; they're unclean until evening.

When she's cleansed from her discharge, she has to count seven days, and then she's clean. On the eighth day, she needs to get two doves or two pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The priest will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest will make things right for her with God because of the discharge that made her unclean.
'You guys are responsible for keeping the Israelites separate from what makes them unclean, so they don't die in their uncleanness by defiling my Dwelling Place that's right there with them.'

'So these are the rules for a guy with a discharge or an emission of semen that makes him unclean, and for a woman on her period—any guy or girl with a discharge, and also for a guy who sleeps with a woman who is unclean.'

title: The Ultimate Reset Button: Day of Atonement
paragraphs: So, after Aaron's two sons died—yeah, they messed up and brought some weird fire to God and died—God talked to Moses. He was like, "Tell your brother Aaron to chill. He can't just barge into the Most Holy Place, behind the curtain in front of the Atonement-Cover on the Ark, whenever he wants. If he does, he'll die. Because I'm right there in the cloud over the Atonement-Cover."

"So here's the deal for when Aaron does go into the Holy Place. He needs to bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. He's gotta wear the special holy linen tunic and underwear, tie the linen sash, and put on the linen turban. These are sacred clothes, so he has to take a bath before he even puts them on. Then, he'll get two male goats from the Israelites for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering.

"Aaron's gotta offer the bull for his own sin offering to make things right for himself and his family. Then he'll take the two goats and present them to God at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. He'll cast lots for the two goats—one lot for God and the other for this goat called Azazel. The goat that gets the 'God' lot, he'll sacrifice as a sin offering. But the goat that gets the 'Azazel' lot will be sent out into the desert to Azazel to take the blame.

"Then Aaron will bring his bull for the sin offering to make things right for himself and his family. He'll slaughter the bull for the sin offering. He'll grab a censer full of hot coals from the altar before God and two handfuls of ground-up fragrant incense. He'll take them behind the curtain and put the incense on the fire in front of God. The smoke from the incense will cover the Atonement-Cover over the Ark of the Covenant so he doesn't die. He'll take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the Atonement-Cover, and then sprinkle the blood in front of it seven times.

"Next, he'll slaughter the goat that was chosen as the sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the curtain. He'll do the same thing he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on and in front of the Atonement-Cover. This is how he'll make the Most Holy Place clean from all the messed-up stuff the Israelites did, all their rebellion and sins. He has to do the same thing for the Tent of Meeting, which is right there in the middle of all their uncleanness. No one is allowed to be in the Tent of Meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make things right in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, after he's made things right for himself, his family, and the whole community of Israel.

"Then he'll go out to the altar that's in front of God and make it clean too. He'll take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and smear it on all four corners of the altar. With his finger, he'll sprinkle some of the blood on it seven times to purify it and make it holy from all the Israelites' junk.

"When Aaron is done cleaning the Most Holy Place, the Tent of Meeting, and the altar, he'll bring out the live goat. He'll put both of his hands on the goat's head and confess all the bad things the Israelites have done, all their rebellious acts, and all their sins. He's basically putting all their sins on the goat's head. Then he'll send it away into the wilderness, led by a guy who's ready to go. The goat will carry all their sins to some empty, deserted place, and the guy will let it go free out there in the wilderness.

"Finally, Aaron will go back into the Tent of Meeting and take off the linen clothes he wore when he went into the Most Holy Place and leave them there. He'll take a bath in a holy place, put on his regular priestly clothes, and then offer the burnt offering for himself and the burnt offering for the people. This makes things right for himself and the people. He'll also burn the fat from the sin offering on the altar.

"The guy who took the goat out to Azazel in the wilderness has to wash his clothes and take a bath. After that, he can come back into the camp. The bull and the goat for the sin offerings, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place to make things right, have to be taken outside the camp and burned—their hides, their meat, and their guts. The guy who burns them has to wash his clothes and take a bath too. Then he can come back into the camp.

"This is a rule you have to follow forever. On the tenth day of the seventh month, everyone—whether you're a citizen or a foreigner living with you—has to fast and not do any work. Because on this day, you'll be made right with God and cleansed. In God's presence, you'll be cleaned of all your sins. It's like the ultimate Sabbath, a day of complete rest. You have to fast. This is a rule forever.
"The priest who is anointed and chosen to take over from his father will be the one to do this atonement ceremony.
He puts on the sacred linen clothes;
He cleanses the Most Holy Place by making atonement;
He cleanses the Tent of Meeting and the Altar by making atonement;
He makes atonement for the priests and the whole community.
"This is a rule for you forever: Once a year, atonement has to be made for all the sins of the people of Israel."
And Aaron did it, exactly as God told Moses.

title: The #1 Rule About Sacrifices
paragraphs: Alright, so God hits up Moses and is like, 'Yo, tell Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites the deal. Here's the command from the big guy: If anyone from now on decides to kill an ox, lamb, or goat, whether they're in the camp or not, they *have* to bring it to the entrance of the main tent, the Tent of Meeting, to offer it to God right there in front of His place. If they don't, that's a major foul. Like, they're guilty of murder, for real. They've shed blood and will get kicked out of the community. The whole point is to get the Israelites to stop doing their own thing and sacrificing animals in random fields. From now on, they gotta bring their sacrifices to God, to the priest at the Tent of Meeting, and do it as a proper Peace-Offering. The priest will then splash the blood on God's altar and burn the fat, which is like a super pleasing smell to God. And another thing, they absolutely have to stop sacrificing to those goat-demon things. That's some weird, culty stuff and it's canceled. This rule is forever, for all time.'

“Also, tell them this: Any Israelite, or even a foreigner hanging with them, who wants to give a big offering, like a Whole-Burnt-Offering or a Peace-Offering, but doesn't bring it to the Tent of Meeting to offer to God? That person is getting cut off from everyone. No exceptions.

“And listen up, this is a big one. If any Israelite or foreigner living with you eats blood, I'm personally disowning them and cutting them off from the people. Here's why: the life of an animal is literally in its blood. I've given you the blood to make things right for your lives on the altar. It's the blood, the life itself, that fixes things. That's why I'm telling all of you, the People of Israel, 'Do not eat blood.' And the same rule applies to any foreigner living with you. Seriously, don't eat blood.

“And for any Israelite, or foreigner for that matter, who goes hunting and catches an animal or bird that's good to eat, they have to drain all the blood out and cover it with dirt. It's because the life of every creature is its blood—the blood is its life. That's why I'm telling the Israelites, 'Don't eat the blood of any animal, because the life of every animal is its blood.' Anyone who eats it will be cut off, period.

“And one last thing. If anyone, whether they're from here or not, eats an animal they just found dead or that was killed by another animal, they need to wash their clothes and take a bath. They'll be considered 'unclean' until the evening, but then they're good. But if they don't wash up, they'll have to face the consequences for their actions.”

title: God's Relationship Rules: The Hard No's
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, “Yo, tell the Israelites, I’m your God, for real. Don’t be copying the Egyptians where you used to live, and definitely don’t act like the Canaanites where I’m taking you. Their way of life is not it. You gotta follow my rules and live by my standards. I’m your God. Stick to my rules, and you’ll actually live. I’m God.
Alright, first thing’s first: don’t get with anyone in your immediate family. I’m God, and I’m serious.
Don’t disrespect your dad by sleeping with your mom. She’s your mom. Just don’t.
Don’t sleep with your dad’s wife. That’s a major violation against your own father.
Don’t get with your sister, whether you share a dad or a mom, or grew up together or not. It’s off-limits.
Don’t sleep with your granddaughter, from your son or your daughter. That’s just messing with your own family line.
Don’t get with your stepsister, the daughter of your dad's wife. She’s your sister, so that’s a no-go.
Don’t sleep with your aunt on your dad’s side. She’s your dad’s close relative.
And don’t sleep with your aunt on your mom’s side. She’s your mom’s close relative.
Don’t disrespect your uncle by getting with his wife. She’s your aunt.
Don’t sleep with your daughter-in-law. She’s your son’s wife, so hands off.
Don’t sleep with your brother’s wife. That’s a betrayal to your brother.
Don’t get with a woman and her daughter. And definitely not her granddaughters either. They’re all close relatives, and that’s just messed up.
And if you're married, don’t marry your wife’s sister to start drama and sleep with her while your wife is still around.
Don’t get with a woman when she’s on her period and unclean.
Don’t sleep with your neighbor’s wife. That’s just wrong and makes you unclean.
And for real, don’t sacrifice any of your kids to the god Molech. That’s like, the ultimate slap in the face to your God. I am God.
Don’t sleep with a guy like you would with a girl. That’s detestable to God.
Don’t get with an animal. That’s perverse.
A woman should never get with an animal. That’s perverse.

Don’t get yourselves all dirty with this stuff. This is how all the other nations I’m about to kick out got so messed up. The land itself got polluted, and I had to punish it. The land literally threw up the people living there. So you guys gotta stick to my rules—whether you were born here or just moved here. Don’t do any of these detestable things. The people who were here before you did all this and polluted the whole place. And if you pollute it, the land will throw you up just like it did to them.

Anyone who does any of these detestable things will be cut off from everyone. Stick to what I tell you. Don’t get into the gross habits of the people who were here before you. Don’t pollute yourselves with them. I’m your God, for real.”

title: God's Top Rules for Living Right
paragraphs: God told Moses, 'Yo, tell the whole crew of Israel, you gotta be holy ‘cause I, your God, am holy.'
'Respect your mom and dad, for real.'
'And keep my Sabbaths. I’m your God, for real for real.'
'Don’t get mixed up with fake gods or idols. Don’t even think about making your own gods. I’m your God.'

'When you make a Peace-Offering to God, do it the right way so it’s accepted. You can eat it on the day you offer it and the next day, but if there’s anything left on the third day, you gotta burn it. If you eat it on the third day, it’s nasty and not cool. Whoever eats it will have to face the consequences for disrespecting what’s holy to God. That person will be kicked out of the community.'

'When you harvest your crops, don’t harvest right up to the edges of your field, and don’t pick up the fallen grain. Don’t strip your vineyard bare or go back for the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am God, your God.'
'No stealing.'
'No lying.'
'Don’t deceive anyone.'
'Don’t use my name to make fake promises, that’s just messed up. I am God.'
'Don’t take advantage of your friends or rob them.'
'Pay your workers on time. Don’t make them wait overnight for their money.'
'Don’t make fun of deaf people or trip blind people. Fear your God. I am God.'
'Don’t be biased in court. Don’t treat poor people or rich people differently. Judge fairly.'
'Don’t spread gossip or rumors.'
'Don’t just stand there when your neighbor’s life is in danger. Do something. I am God.'
'If you have a problem with someone, talk to them about it. Don’t just hate them in secret. That makes you part of the problem.'
'Don’t try to get revenge or hold a grudge against any of your people.
Love your neighbor as yourself. I am God.'
'Follow my rules.'
'Don’t breed two different kinds of animals.'
'Don’t plant two different kinds of seeds in your fields.'
'Don’t wear clothes made of two different kinds of fabric.'

'If a man sleeps with a slave girl who’s engaged to someone else but hasn’t been freed or ransomed yet, there has to be an investigation. But they won’t be put to death because she wasn’t free. The man has to bring a Compensation-Offering to God at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting—a ram. The priest will perform the atonement ritual for him before God with the ram for the sin he committed. Then he’ll be forgiven for the sin he committed.'

'When you plant a fruit tree, don’t eat the fruit for the first three years. In the fourth year, the fruit is a holy offering to God. From the fifth year on, you can eat the fruit. This way, you’ll have even bigger harvests. I am God, your God.'
'Don’t eat meat with blood in it.'
'Don’t mess with fortune-telling or witchcraft.'
'Don’t get weird haircuts or shave your beard in a strange way.'
'Don’t cut your bodies for the dead.'
'Don’t get tattoos. I am God.'
'Don’t turn your daughter into a prostitute. That would mess up the whole country.'
'Keep my Sabbaths and respect my holy place. I am God.'
'Don’t get involved with ghosts or spirits. It will mess up your soul. I am God, your God.'
'Show respect to old people. Honor them. Fear your God. I am God.'

'If a foreigner comes to live in your land, don’t take advantage of them. Treat them the same as you would your own people. Love them like you love yourself. Remember that you were once foreigners in Egypt. I am God, your God.'
'Don’t cheat when you’re measuring things. Use honest scales and weights. I am God, your God. I’m the one who brought you out of Egypt.'
'So, follow all my rules and laws. Seriously, do it. I am God.'
