title: God's Rules: These Are Serious
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, “Alright, tell the Israelites, every single one of them, and any foreigner hanging with them: if you give your kid to the fake god Molech, you’re done. The whole community has to take you out by stoning. This is serious.

I’ll straight-up reject that person and cut them off from everyone. By giving their kid to Molech, they’ve trashed my holy place and disrespected my holy name. And if the community just pretends they didn’t see it and lets the person get away with it, I’m gonna step in. I’ll reject that person, their whole family, and anyone else who joined in on the messed-up Molech rituals. I’ll cut them all off.
“I’m also going to reject anyone messing with psychics or mediums, basically cheating on me with that stuff. I’ll cut them off from the community too.
“So, for real, set yourselves apart and live a holy life. Be holy, because I’m your God. Just do what I say. Live how I tell you. I’m the God who makes you holy.
“And look, anyone who curses their dad or mom has to be put to death. If you curse your parents, you’ve got no one to blame but yourself.
“If a guy cheats on his wife with another man’s wife, like his neighbor’s, both the guy and the girl have to be put to death. End of story.
“If a guy sleeps with his stepmom, he’s disrespected his own dad. Both of them have to be put to death. They brought it on themselves.
“If a guy sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them have to be put to death. What they did was twisted, and they’re responsible for their own deaths.
“If a man has sex with another man the way you would with a woman, they’ve both committed a detestable act. They have to be put to death; their blood is on their own hands.
“If a man marries a woman and her mother, that’s depraved. All three of them have to be burned to death to purge that evil from the community.
“If a guy has sex with an animal, he has to be put to death, and you have to kill the animal too.
“If a woman has sex with an animal, you have to kill both the woman and the animal. They have to be put to death, and they’re responsible for their own deaths.

“If a guy marries his sister, from either his dad’s or mom’s side, and they sleep together, that’s a total disgrace. They have to be publicly kicked out of the community. He’s violated his sister and has to face the consequences.
“If a guy sleeps with a woman when she’s on her period, he’s messed with her flow and she’s shared it. Both of them have to be cut off from the community.
“Don’t sleep with your aunt, on either your mom’s or dad’s side. That’s a violation of a close relative. You’ll both be held responsible.
“If a guy sleeps with his aunt, he’s dishonored his uncle. They’ll be held responsible and won’t have kids.
“If a guy marries his brother’s wife, that’s just wrong. He’s shamed his brother. They won’t have kids.

“So do what I tell you, all my rules and laws. Live by them so the land I’m giving you doesn’t get sick of you and throw you up. You absolutely cannot live like the other nations I’m kicking out for you. They did all this stuff, and I hated every second of it.

“But I told you, remember, that you’re gonna get their land. I’m giving it to you, a land that’s awesome, flowing with milk and honey. I’m your God, and I’ve set you apart from all the other nations. So act like it. Know the difference between clean and unclean animals and birds. Don’t make yourselves gross with any animal or bird or bug that I’ve told you is unclean.
“Live holy lives for me, because I, God, am holy. I’ve set you apart from all the other nations to be my special people.
“Any man or woman who is a medium or a sorcerer has to be put to death. You have to stone them. They’re responsible for their own deaths.”

title: The Holiness Code: Rules for God's Crew
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and was like, “Yo, tell the priests, Aaron’s sons, the deal. A priest can’t just make himself spiritually unclean by touching a dead body. The only exceptions are your immediate family: your mom, dad, son, daughter, brother, or a sister who isn’t married and still depends on you. For them, it’s okay to get unclean. But for anyone else, like your in-laws? Nah. That just makes you look bad and desecrates your role.

“Also, priests can’t be shaving their heads in weird ways, trimming their beards, or cutting their bodies. They have to be holy for their God and not drag God's name through the mud. Because their main gig is presenting God's gifts—God's food—they have to be holy.

“Because a priest is set apart for God, he can't marry a woman who's been a prostitute, a shrine prostitute, or is divorced. You gotta see him as holy because he serves the food of your God. Treat him as holy because I, God, who make you holy, am holy myself.

“And this is super serious: if a priest’s daughter messes up and gets into prostitution, she’s not just disgracing herself, she’s disgracing her father. She has to be burned at the stake. It's that big of a deal.

“The head priest, the one who got the special oil poured on his head and wears the official gear, has even stricter rules. He can’t let his hair get all messy, and he can’t wear torn clothes. He can't even go into a room with a dead body. He can't make himself unclean, not even for his own mom or dad. He can't just ditch the Sanctuary of his God or treat it like it's nothing, because he's been set apart by the anointing oil. I am God.

“He has to marry a young virgin. Not a widow, not a divorced woman, not a former prostitute. He has to marry a virgin from his own people. He can’t mess up his family line among his people, because I am the God who makes him holy.”

Then God said to Moses, “Tell Aaron this: None of your descendants, for all time, who has a disqualifying physical condition can offer up the food of his God. That means anyone who’s blind or has trouble walking, has a facial difference or an injured body part, a damaged foot or hand, a curved back or short stature, an eye condition, painful skin sores, or a genital injury. No descendant of Aaron the priest with such a condition can present gifts to God. Because of his condition, he can't offer the food of his God. He can still eat God's food, both the super holy and the regular holy stuff, but because of his condition, he can't go near the special curtain or the Altar. That would desecrate my Sanctuary. I am the God who makes them holy.”
So Moses told all this to Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel.

title: God's Rules for Offerings: The Dos and Don'ts
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Yo, tell Aaron and his sons to be super careful with the holy offerings the Israelites give me. They can't be disrespecting my holy name. I'm God, for real."
"Tell them, from now on, if any of their future kids come near the holy offerings while they're 'unclean,' they're basically kicked out of my presence. I'm God, and I'm not playing."

"Every single one of Aaron's descendants who has a serious skin condition or a discharge can't eat any of the holy offerings until he's clean. Also, if he touches anything defiled by a dead body, or has a wet dream, or touches a creepy crawly, or touches someone who's unclean for whatever reason—if you touch any of that stuff, you're unclean until evening and you can't eat any of the holy offerings unless you wash up real good. After the sun goes down, he's clean and can go ahead and eat the holy offerings; they're his food. But he can't make himself unclean by eating roadkill or something a wild animal got to. I am God."
"The priests have to follow my rules, or they'll be found guilty and die for treating the offerings like they're nothing. I am God, and I'm the one who makes them holy."

"No regular person can eat anything that's set apart as holy. Not even a priest's guest or his hired worker can eat holy stuff. But if a priest buys a slave, that slave can eat it; and the slaves born in his house can eat his food too. If a priest's daughter marries a regular guy, she can't eat from the holy contributions anymore. But if the priest's daughter is widowed or divorced and doesn't have any kids and moves back into her dad's house like before, she can eat her dad's food. But no regular person can eat it."
"If someone accidentally eats a holy offering, he has to give it back to the priest and add twenty percent to it."

"The priests can't be treating the holy offerings from the Israelites like they're nothing, or they'll mess up and make themselves guilty when they eat the holy offerings. I am God, the one who makes them holy."

God told Moses, "Tell Aaron and his sons and all the people of Israel, every single one of you, whether you were born here or you're a foreigner, when you bring a whole-burnt-offering to God to keep a promise or just because you want to, you have to make sure it's a male with no defects from your cattle, sheep, or goats for it to be accepted. Don't even try to slip in some animal that has something wrong with it—it won't be accepted. Whenever anyone brings an offering from cattle or sheep as a peace-offering to God to keep a promise or just because you want to, it has to be perfect, with no defects, to be accepted. Don't try giving God an animal that's blind, crippled, mutilated, or has gross sores, a rash, or mange. Don't put any of those on the altar as a gift to God. You can, however, offer an ox or sheep that's a little deformed or stunted as a freewill-offering, but it's not okay for keeping a promise. And don't offer God an animal with bruised, crushed, torn, or cut-off testicles. Don't do that in your own land, and don't take them from foreigners and offer them as food for your God either. Because of their deformities and defects, they won't be accepted."

God told Moses, "When a calf or lamb or goat is born, it has to stay with its mom for seven days. After the eighth day, it's good to go as an offering, a gift to God. Don't slaughter a cow or ewe and its baby on the same day. When you sacrifice a thanksgiving-offering to God, do it right so it will be accepted. Eat it on the same day; don't leave any leftovers until morning. I am God."
"Do what I say; live by what I say. I am God."
"Don't trash my holy name. I demand to be treated with holy respect among the people of Israel. I am God who makes you holy and brought you out of Egypt to be your God. I am God."

title: God's Official Holiday Schedule
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, "Yo, tell the people of Israel, these are my official holidays, the ones you gotta announce as special holy meetups.
Work for six days, but the seventh day is the Sabbath. That means total and complete rest, a holy get-together. Don't do any work. Wherever you're living, it's a Sabbath for God.
So here's the list of God's official holidays, the sacred meetups you need to schedule at the right times:
First up, God's Passover. It starts at sundown on the fourteenth day of the first month.

Then comes God's Feast of Unraised Bread, on the fifteenth day of the same month. For seven days, you're only eating bread made without yeast. The first day is a holy meetup; no regular work. You'll give special fire-gifts to God for seven days. On the seventh day, have another holy meetup and, again, no regular work."

God spoke to Moses again: "Tell the Israelites, when you get to the land I'm giving you and you harvest your crops, bring the priest a bundle of the very first grain you harvest. He'll wave it in front of God so He'll accept it on your behalf. The priest will do this the morning after the Sabbath. On that same day, you'll offer a perfect one-year-old male lamb as a big burnt offering to God. With it, you'll give a grain offering of four quarts of fine flour mixed with oil—a fire-gift for God that smells amazing—and also a drink offering of a quart of wine. Don't eat any bread, or roasted or fresh grain until you've given this offering to your God. This is a rule that lasts forever for all your future generations, no matter where you live.

Next, you're gonna count seven full weeks from the morning after the Sabbath when you brought the grain bundle as a wave offering. That's fifty days until the morning of the seventh Sabbath. Then, you'll present a new grain offering to God. From wherever you live, bring two loaves of bread made from four quarts of fine flour, baked with yeast, as a wave offering of the first ripe grain for God. Along with the bread, offer seven perfect yearling male lambs, one bull, and two rams. They'll be a huge burnt offering to God, along with their grain and drink offerings—fire-gifts that smell awesome to God. Also, offer one male goat to say you're sorry for your sins and two yearling lambs as a peace offering. The priest will wave the two lambs before God as a wave offering, along with the bread from the first ripe grain. They are holy offerings to God that belong to the priest. Announce that day as a holy meetup. No regular work. This is a forever rule wherever you live, for all your generations.
And when you're harvesting your land, don't be greedy and harvest every last bit. Leave the corners of your field and any dropped stalks for the poor and for foreigners. I am God, your God."

God then said to Moses: "Tell the people of Israel, on the first day of the seventh month, you're to have a day of rest, a holy meetup—you'll mark it with loud blasts from a ram's horn. Don't do any regular work. Just offer a fire-gift to God."

God also said to Moses: "The tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement. You'll have a holy meetup, you'll fast, and you'll offer a fire-gift to God. Don't work at all that day because it's the day when things are made right for you before your God. Anyone who doesn't fast on that day gets cut off from the community. And I'll personally get rid of anyone who works on that day. So, no work. None. This is a forever rule for all your generations, wherever you end up living. It's a Sabbath of complete and total rest, a day of fasting. You'll observe your Sabbath from the evening of the ninth day of the month until the next evening."

God said to Moses: "Tell the Israelites, God's Feast of Booths kicks off on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. It goes for seven days. The first day is a holy meetup; no regular work. You'll offer fire-gifts to God for seven days. On the eighth day, have another holy meetup and offer a gift to God. It's a big, serious gathering. No regular work.

So, these are God's official holidays that you'll announce as holy meetups for giving fire-gifts to God: the big burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and drink offerings for each specific day. These are on top of the offerings for God's Sabbaths and any other gifts you've promised or just feel like giving to God.

So, to sum it up: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you've gathered all your crops, you'll celebrate the Feast of God for seven days. The first day is a total chill day, and the eighth day is also a total chill day. On the first day, grab the best fruit from the best trees, get some palm fronds, branches from leafy trees, and willows from the creek, and just celebrate with your God for seven days—yep, a full seven-day festival for God. Every year from now on, celebrate it in the seventh month. You'll live in little huts or booths for seven days—every single person in Israel is to move into these booths. This is so your kids and their kids will know that I had the people of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of Egypt. I am God, your God."
Moses then posted the calendar for all of God's official holidays that Israel was supposed to celebrate.

title: Don't Disrespect The Name
paragraphs: God told Moses, "Tell the Israelites to bring you top-quality olive oil for the light, so the lamps can stay lit all the time. Aaron's job is to keep these lamps burning from evening till morning before God, right in front of the curtain that hides the Ark of the Covenant. This is a rule forever, for all your descendants. Aaron is in charge of keeping the lamps on the pure gold lampstand burning before God, always."

"Then, take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using about four quarts of flour for each loaf. Arrange them in two rows, six in each, on the pure gold table before God. Put some pure incense along each row to represent the bread as a memorial offering, a gift to God. Every Sabbath day, this bread needs to be set before God regularly. It's a permanent promise from the people of Israel. Afterwards, the bread belongs to Aaron and his sons. They have to eat it in a holy place because it's their super holy share of the gifts given to God. This is a permanent rule."

So, one day, this guy whose mom was an Israelite and whose dad was Egyptian was hanging out with the Israelites, and he got into a fight with an Israelite man in the camp. During the fight, the son of the Israelite woman blasphemed God's name and cursed. They took him to Moses. (His mom's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.) They put him in jail, waiting to find out what God wanted them to do.

Then God spoke to Moses, "Take the guy who blasphemed outside the camp. Have everyone who heard him put their hands on his head, and then the whole community has to stone him to death. And tell the Israelites: Anyone who curses their God will be held responsible. Anyone who blasphemes God's name must be executed. The whole community has to stone them. It doesn't matter if they're a foreigner or a native—if they blaspheme the Name, they die."

"If someone attacks and kills another person, they must be put to death. If someone kills another person's animal, they have to pay it back—a life for a life. If you injure your neighbor, you get the same injury back: a fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever injury they caused, the same will be done to them. So, if you kill an animal, you pay it back, but if you kill a person, you're put to death. There are no double standards; the same rule applies to foreigners and natives alike. I am God, your God."
Moses then told all this to the Israelites. They brought the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. The people of Israel did exactly what God had commanded Moses.

title: The Ultimate Reset Button: Jubilee Year!
paragraphs: God hit up Moses on Mount Sinai and was like, "Yo, tell the Israelites, when you get to the land I'm giving you, the land itself is gonna get a Sabbath for God. For six years, you can plant your fields, trim your vineyards, and bring in your crops. But that seventh year? The land gets a full-on Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath for God. You can't plant your fields or trim your vineyards. Don't even harvest the stuff that grows by itself; don't pick the grapes from your wild vines. The land gets a whole year of total chill. But you can totally eat whatever the land serves up on its own during that Sabbath year—you, your servants, your hired workers, the foreigners living with you, and yeah, even your cattle and the wild animals. Whatever the land gives, you can eat."

"Count off seven of those Sabbath years—so, seven times seven years, which is 49 years. Then, on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement, you gotta blast the ram's horn super loud all over the country. Make the 50th year a holy year. Announce freedom for everyone living in the land—it's a Jubilee for you. Every single person gets to go back to their family's property and link up with their extended family again. The 50th year is your Jubilee year, so no planting, no harvesting the volunteer crops, and no picking from the wild vines because it's the Jubilee and it's a holy year for you. You're allowed to eat whatever grows on its own in the fields."
"In this Jubilee year, everyone goes back home to their family's land."

"If you sell or buy land from one of your own people, don't rip them off. You gotta figure out the price based on how many years it's been since the last Jubilee. And the seller has to set the price based on how many harvests are left until the next Jubilee. The more years left, the higher the price. But the fewer years left, the lower the price. What you're really buying and selling is the number of crops you're gonna get. So don't cheat each other. Fear your God. I am God, your God."

"Stick to my rules and follow my laws, and you'll live securely in the land. The land will produce its fruit, you'll have more than enough to eat, and you'll be safe and sound. And if you're thinking, 'What are we gonna eat in the seventh year if we don't plant or harvest?' I'm telling you, I'll send such a huge blessing in the sixth year that the land will produce enough for three whole years. While you're planting in the eighth year, you'll still be eating the old food and you'll keep eating it until the harvest of the ninth year comes in."
"The land can't be sold forever, because the land is mine and you're just foreigners—you're my tenants. You have to make sure there's a way to buy back any land that you own."

"If one of your relatives becomes poor and has to sell some of their land, their closest family member should come and buy back what they sold. If someone doesn't have anyone to buy it back, but then they get successful and make enough money to buy it back themselves, they need to calculate the value since they sold it and give the rest of the money back to the person they sold it to. Then they can go back to their own land. If they can't get enough money together to pay it back, what they sold stays with the buyer until the Jubilee year. In the Jubilee, it will be returned and they can go back and live on their land."

"If someone sells a house in a walled city, they have the right to buy it back for a whole year after the sale. They can redeem it anytime during that year. But if it's not bought back before the year is over, it becomes the permanent property of the buyer and their family. It doesn't get returned in the Jubilee. However, houses in villages without walls are treated the same as fields. They can be bought back and have to be returned at the Jubilee."

"When it comes to the Levite cities, houses in the cities owned by the Levites can always be bought back. Levite property can always be redeemed if it's sold in a town they own, and it goes back to them in the Jubilee, because the houses in the Levite towns are their property among the Israelites. The pastures that belong to their cities can't be sold; they're their permanent property."

"If one of your relatives becomes poor and can't support themselves, you have to help them out, just like you would a foreigner or a guest, so they can keep living in your community. Don't scam them with high interest rates; out of respect for your God, help your relative keep living with you. Don't take advantage of their bad situation by charging crazy interest on their loans, and don't sell them food to make a profit. I am your God who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God."

"If one of your relatives becomes so poor that they have to sell themselves to you, don't treat them like a slave. Treat them like a hired worker or a guest. They'll work for you until the Jubilee, and after that, they and their children are set free to go back to their family and their ancestral land. Because the Israelites are my servants who I brought out of Egypt, they must never be sold as slaves. Don't be a tyrant to them; fear your God."

"Your male and female slaves have to come from the nations around you; you're allowed to buy slaves from them. You can also buy the kids of foreign workers who are living with you temporarily and from their families who are living with you and were born in your land. They become your property. You can pass them down to your children as property and make them slaves for life. But you must not be a tyrant to your fellow Israelites."

"If a foreigner or a temporary resident living with you gets rich and one of your relatives becomes poor and sells themselves to that foreigner or to a member of the foreigner's family, they still have the right to be bought back after they've sold themselves. One of their relatives can buy them back. An uncle or a cousin or any close relative can redeem them. Or, if they get the money together, they can buy themselves back. What happens then is they and their owner figure out the time from the year they sold themselves to the Jubilee year; the buy-back price is based on a hired worker's wages for that many years. If there are a lot of years left before the Jubilee, they have to pay back a bigger part of their purchase price, but if there are only a few years left until the Jubilee, they figure out the price accordingly. They should be treated like someone hired year by year. You have to make sure their owner doesn't treat them like a tyrant."

"If they're not bought back in any of these ways, they go free in the Jubilee year, them and their children, because the Israelites are my servants, my servants whom I brought out of Egypt. I am God, your God."

title: The Ultimate 'Follow the Rules' Challenge
paragraphs: “Alright, listen up. Don’t go making your own little gods, setting up statues or sacred stones to bow down to. I’m your God, and that’s final.
“Make sure you keep my Sabbaths, and show some respect for my Sanctuary. I’m God.

“If you actually live by my rules and follow my commands, I’ll make sure the rain comes when it should, the ground will give you amazing crops, and the trees will be loaded with fruit. You’ll be harvesting grain all the way to grape season, and picking grapes right up until you need to plant again. You’ll have more than enough food and can chill out, safe and sound in your own land.

“I’ll make your country a peaceful place. You’ll be able to sleep without worrying about a thing. I’ll get rid of any dangerous animals and stop any wars from happening. You’ll chase off your enemies and totally own them. Like, five of you will make a hundred of them run, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand. I’ll be looking out for you, making sure you thrive and your population grows, and I’ll keep my promises to you. You’ll have so much food left over from last year that you’ll have to clear it out to make space for the new stuff.

“I’ll come and live in your neighborhood. I won’t ghost you or avoid you. I’ll walk around with you. I’ll be your God, and you’ll be my people. I’m the God who personally rescued you from Egypt so you wouldn’t be slaves anymore. I broke the chains of your slavery so you can walk tall and be free.

“But, if you ignore me and don’t follow my commands, if you hate my rules and disrespect my laws, basically trashing our agreement, then I’m going to have to step in and bring the drama. I’m talking serious sickness, burning fevers, blindness, and your life just draining away. You’ll plant crops, but your enemies will be the ones eating them. I’ll turn my back on you, and you’ll get crushed by your enemies. People who hate you will be in charge. You’ll be running scared even when no one is chasing you.

“And if that doesn’t get your attention, I’ll have to discipline you seven times worse for your sins. I’ll shatter your pride. The sky will be like a metal roof and the ground like hard iron. You’ll work like crazy, but nothing will grow. No crops, no fruit.

“If you still defy me and refuse to listen, your punishment will get seven times worse. I’ll send wild animals to attack you. They’ll snatch your kids, kill your cattle, and your population will drop so much it’ll feel like a ghost town.

“And if even *that* doesn’t work and you keep ignoring my discipline and defying me, then I’ll have to defy you back. I, myself, will punish you seven times over for your sins. I’ll unleash war on you to get back at you for breaking our deal. When you’re all hiding in your cities, I’ll send a plague, and you’ll be totally helpless. When I cut off your food supply, ten women will have to share one oven and hand out bread in tiny rations. You’ll eat, but you’ll still be starving.

“And if—get this—even *that* doesn’t work and you still won’t listen, still defy me, I’ll lose it. In my anger, I’ll defy you, punishing you seven times over. The famine will be so insane that you’ll end up doing the unthinkable—cooking and eating your own sons and daughters. I’ll destroy all your pagan shrines and the junk that goes with them, and I’ll pile your dead bodies on top of your worthless idols. I’ll be disgusted by you. I’ll turn your cities into wastelands and wreck your holy places. I won’t be interested in your sacrifices anymore. I’ll make your land so desolate that even your enemies who take it over will be shocked. I’ll scatter you across the world and hunt you down. Your land will be empty, your cities deserted. With you gone, the land will finally get a break and enjoy its rest years. All the time it’s empty, it will get the rest it never got when you were living there.

“As for the survivors, I’ll make them so paranoid that even the sound of a leaf blowing in the wind will make them freak out. They’ll run for their lives even when no one is chasing them, tripping over each other in chaos. You won’t be able to stand up to your enemies. You’ll die in foreign lands; the land of your enemies will swallow you up. Whoever is left will waste away because of their sins, and the sins of their ancestors.

“But, on the other hand, if they confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors—how they betrayed me and defied me, which made me defy them and send them away; if they finally humble their stubborn hearts and accept the punishment for their sin, then I’ll remember my promise to Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. And I’ll remember the land.

“The land will be empty, enjoying its rest while they’re gone. They’ll pay for their sins because they rejected my laws and hated my rules. But even then, while they’re in their enemies’ lands, I won’t completely reject or destroy them. I won’t break my promise to them, because I am their God. For their sake, I’ll remember the promise I made to their ancestors, who I brought out of Egypt while all the other nations watched, so that I could be their God. I am God.”
These are the rules, laws, and instructions that God set up between himself and the people of Israel, through Moses at Mount Sinai.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Making Deals with God
paragraphs: God hit up Moses and said, "Alright, tell the Israelites the deal. If someone wants to make a vow to God by dedicating the value of a person, here's the price list. A guy from 20 to 60 is worth 50 silver shekels, and a woman is 30 shekels. If they're between 5 and 20, it's 20 shekels for a guy and 10 for a girl. For the little ones, from one month to five years old, a boy is 5 silver shekels and a girl is 3. If they're over 60, a man is 15 shekels and a woman is 10. But hey, if someone's too broke to pay that, they just show the person to the priest, and the priest will set a fair price based on what the person making the vow can actually afford."

"Now, if you vow an animal that's legit for an offering to God, that animal is God's, period. It becomes sanctuary property. You can't swap it out—no trading a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If you try to pull a fast one and substitute it, both the original animal and the substitute become holy property. If you vowed an animal that's not clean, one you can't offer to God, you have to show it to the priest. He'll decide its value, high or low. Whatever the priest says, goes. If the owner has second thoughts and wants to buy it back, they have to add an extra 20% to its value."

"If you dedicate your house to God, making it sanctuary property, the priest checks it out and sets the price, high or low. Whatever value the priest puts on it, that's the final word. If the guy who dedicated it wants to buy it back, he has to pay the price plus an extra 20%, and then it's his again."

"If someone dedicates a piece of their family's land to God, its value is based on how much seed it needs. The rate is 50 silver shekels for every six bushels of barley seed. If he dedicates the field during the Year of Jubilee, that price is locked in. But if it's after the Jubilee, the priest has to calculate the value based on how many years are left until the next Jubilee, and the price goes down. If the person who dedicated it wants to buy it back, they have to add 20% to its value, and it's theirs again. But if they don't buy it back, or if they sell it to someone else, it can never be redeemed. When the field is released in the Jubilee year, it becomes holy to God, like, it's literally God's field and belongs to the priests."

"If a man dedicates a field he bought—one that wasn't originally his family's land—the priest will figure out its value based on the time left until the next Jubilee. The guy has to pay that amount on the spot, and it becomes holy to God. Then, in the Year of Jubilee, the land goes back to the original owner he bought it from. All these valuations are based on the official sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs."

"Also, you can't dedicate the firstborn of an animal. The firstborn already belongs to God by default, whether it's a cow or a sheep. It's already His. If it's an unclean animal, the owner can buy it back at its assessed value plus 20%. If he doesn't redeem it, it gets sold at its assessed value."

"But, for real, anything a person *irrevocably* devotes to God—whether it's a person, an animal, or family land—can't be sold or bought back. Ever. Anything devoted like that is super holy; it's God's property, no take-backs."
"Any human who has been devoted to destruction can't be redeemed. They have to be put to death."

"A tenth of everything the land produces, whether it's grain from the field or fruit from the trees, belongs to God. It's holy to God. If you want to buy back any of that tenth you've given, you have to add 20% to its value. And for your herds and flocks, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's staff is holy to God. You're not allowed to cherry-pick the good ones or swap them out. If you try to cheat and make a substitution, both the original and the substitute become holy property and can't be bought back."
These are the commands God gave Moses on Mount Sinai for all the people of Israel.
